description: Seradata, formerly known as SpaceTrak, is a commercial database of every orbital launch attempt and every satellite since Sputnik, widely used by launch providers, satellite operators and manufacturers, insurers, space agencies and universities. For each launch and spacecraft it gives the mission, operator, manufacturer, platform, orbit and status, and it tracks launch failures, in-orbit anomalies and failures and satellite insurance claims, recording for each the underlying cause, the phase of flight when it occurred and the equipment at fault. Search results describe coverage of on-orbit anomalies and failures of more than 7,000 spacecraft. The database traces back to printed records, was relaunched as SpaceTrak in 1997, moved online in 2005 and received its current platform in 2015; the UK company Seradata was bought by Slingshot Aerospace in 2022, and the data are updated daily. Coverage: worldwide, 1957 to present. Format and access: online platform with reporting tools under a 12-month paid subscription; articles and summaries are free. Caveats: proprietary; causes of failures are often inferred from public statements; no open licence. Simulation uses: reliability and failure rates of satellites and subsystems for resilience models of space-based services, insurance-loss scenarios and supply-chain dependence on manufacturers. Related records: the NOAA anomaly archive, ESA DISCOS and CelesTrak cover anomalies and objects from open sources.
